BeforeCombatStart.rationale: MeatOnTheBone.cs:24-31 does exactly one thing -- `base.Status = RelicStatus.Active` when the heal would currently fire -- and assigns no gameplay state. RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShouldFlashOnPlayer / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / CanonicalVars' display side / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim. Checked against PROMPT.md bug class 13 and sweep A: this is an override with NO assignment other than the display flag (the very defect batch 6 found in sweep A's old 'C# resets' column), so there is no dropped reset here and the relic holds no per-combat state at all -- it recomputes the threshold from live HP every time.

AfterCurrentHpChanged.rationale: MeatOnTheBone.cs:33-45 likewise assigns only `base.Status`, gated on the creature being the owner and combat being in progress. RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShouldFlashOnPlayer / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / CanonicalVars' display side / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim. It exists so the relic bar lights up live as the player's HP crosses 50%; nothing reads it.

AfterCombatVictoryEarly.maps_to: on_combat_end (meat_on_the_bone.py:17-23), the sim's single combat-end pass
AfterCombatVictoryEarly.issue: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4. Every guard and both constants are faithful (N1-N3); the divergence is that C# runs this relic in a SEPARATE, EARLIER complete pass over all listeners and the sim folds it into the one on_combat_end pass in relic order, so Burning Blood's heal moves the HP above the threshold first.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): AfterCombatVictoryEarly is a SEPARATE, EARLIER full pass in C# and this relic is the ONLY implementer in the whole game; the sim's single on_combat_end pass lets Burning Blood heal first and push the HP above the 50% threshold
guards.issue: MECHANISM: Hook.AfterCombatVictory (Hook.cs:340-351) makes TWO complete passes over `runState.IterateHookListeners` -- every listener's AfterCombatVictoryEarly first, then every listener's AfterCombatVictory. MeatOnTheBone is the sole AfterCombatVictoryEarly override anywhere under src/Core/Models/ (verified by grep), so its threshold test `CurrentHp <= (int)(MaxHp * 50/100)` (MeatOnTheBone.cs:47-58, 60-65) always sees the PRE-heal HP. The sim has one flat `on_combat_end` dispatch (hooks.py:271-275) in RunState.relics order, and the three other ported implementers -- burning_blood.py:15 (+6), black_blood.py:17 (+12) and chosen_cheese.py:19 (+1 Max HP and a heal) -- are all AfterCombatVictory/AfterCombatEnd relics that C# guarantees run SECOND. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py tools/audit/relic_probes_b09.py b09-meat-bone): at 38/80 (threshold 40), the relic alone heals to 50; relic order [burning_blood, meat_on_the_bone] gives 44 and [meat_on_the_bone, burning_blood] gives 56, where C# gives 56 in BOTH cases -- a 12 HP divergence from listener order alone. And the losing order is the one that actually happens: Burning Blood is the Ironclad STARTER relic, granted by start_run, so it is index 0 of RunState.relics and always registers before any relic picked up later. Both sides ported and obtainable: Meat on the Bone is Rare in the transcribed grab bag (relic_pools.py:96), Burning Blood is in every run, and ending a fight between 41% and 50% of max HP is an ordinary outcome. Same FAMILY as audits/seam/turn_structure.json guard G12 (C# guarantees ordering with separate complete passes; the sim flattens them into registration-order luck) and carries that record's `gap` verdict per binding rule 3 -- but a DISTINCT site: G12 covers the turn-boundary hooks, this is the combat-victory pair, and neither the seam record nor any sweep reaches it. Rule 7: leans on hooks.py, Hook.cs, burning_blood.py, black_blood.py and chosen_cheese.py, none hashed here.

guards.rationale: Both truncate toward zero, and for non-negative operands `(int)(m * 0.5)` and `m * 50 // 100` agree for every m (odd max HP included: 75 -> 37 both ways, 81 -> 40 both ways). The constants are the DynamicVar defaults -- `DynamicVar("HpThreshold", 50m)` and `HealVar(12m)` (MeatOnTheBone.cs:18-22) -- with no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file, so 50 and 12 are the non-ascension values and match HP_THRESHOLD_PCT = 50 and HEAL = 12. Both C# reads use `.BaseValue`, so no hook can move them. Comparison is `<=` on both sides (`CurrentHp <= num` vs `self.player.hp <= threshold`), so exactly 50% heals.

Mirrored, and non-vacuous: the sim's on_combat_end fires from _end_combat (combat.py:347-350) on defeats too, and the sim has paths that end a combat with a dead player and player_won=False (combat.py:309). The same guard is present in the three sibling combat-end relics.

guards.what: N3: the hook fires only on VICTORY in C#; the sim's on_combat_end fires on any conclusion and the port re-derives the restriction
guards.rationale: AfterCombatVictoryEarly is dispatched only from Hook.AfterCombatVictory (Hook.cs:340-351), itself called only from CombatManager.cs:999 on the victory path. The port's `if not player_won: return` (meat_on_the_bone.py:18) reconstructs exactly that. Distinct from relic/chosen_cheese, whose C# hook is the any-conclusion AfterCombatEnd and whose port therefore does NOT check player_won -- worth stating side by side, because the two ports look inconsistent and both are right.

guards.what: N4: WillHealOnCombatFinished is RE-EVALUATED inside AfterCombatVictoryEarly (MeatOnTheBone.cs:52) rather than reusing the cached RelicStatus
guards.rationale: So the status flag really is display-only and the decision is always taken from live HP; meat_on_the_bone.py:20-21 likewise recomputes the threshold at combat end. This is what makes the two `base.Status` waivers above safe -- had the heal branched on the cached status, dropping the status updates would have been a gap.
